questions.text: Suppose  a database schedule S involves transactions T1,...,Tn. Construct the precedence graph of S with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If S is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?
questions.solution:
Each edge [latex]T_i\rightarrow T_j[/latex] means [latex]T_i[/latex] must come first. A serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph, and any topological order respects every edge, so it gives an equivalent serial schedule.

Answer: Topological order

questions.text:
Consider the following two phase locking protocol. Suppose a transaction T accesses (for read or write operations), a certain set of objects {O1,... ,Ok}. This is done in the following manner:
Step 1. T acquires exclusive locks to O1,...,Ok in increasing order of their addresses.
Step 2. The required operations are performed.
Step 3. All locks are released.
This protocol will
questions.solution:
All locks are taken before any operation and released only at the end [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a two-phase locking schedule [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] serializable.

Locks are always requested in increasing address order, so no circular wait can form [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock-free.

Answer: guarantee serializability and deadlock-freedom

questions.text:
A database of resear charticles in a journal uses the following schema.

Which is the weakest normal form that the new database satisfies,but the old one does not?
questions.solution:
Old schema: key (VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE), and (VOLUME, NUMBER) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] YEAR is a partial dependency (part of the key determines a non-key attribute) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] only 1NF.

New schemas: YEAR moves to (VOLUME, NUMBER, YEAR), so the partial dependency is gone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2NF (in fact both are in BCNF).

The weakest form the new one satisfies but the old one does not is 2NF.

Answer: 2NF

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the ACID properties of database transactions?
questions.solution:
ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Deadlock-freedom is not one of them.

Answer: Deadlock-freedom

questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT a superkey in a relational schema with attributes
V,W, X, Y, Z and primary key V Y?
questions.solution:
A superkey must contain the whole primary key {V, Y}.
VWXZ has V but no Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not a superkey. The others all contain both V and Y.

Answer: VWXZ
